items.explanation: 48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure 1, hypertension 1; age 48 = 0, no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease, male). Current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only - there is no current anticoagulant order and none has ever been prescribed in clinic. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation in the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, so this untreated AF needs prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is current, most recently reordered 7/18/2026 and valid to 12/26/2026; it was in fact started on 5/14/2024 after this ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable'. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026). Prescriber review of escitalopram, with a repeat ECG, is required.

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 507 ms and Bazett QTc 548 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Citalopram 40 mg daily - a QT watch-list drug, and a dose above the 20 mg maximum advised in older/at-risk patients - is current (order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The memo in force for starts on or after 9/1/2025 requires an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. Because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The revised memo applies to starts on or after 3/1/2026 and requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. The revised memo (starts on or after 3/1/2026) requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not obtained until 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met in time and is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. No ECG is present in the chart. However the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 (5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, would fall inside the window, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start; no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), hypertension (1), age 80 (2), type 2 diabetes (1), prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual hemiplegia and dysarthria (2), old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis (1), female (1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant is ordered. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF - oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated and this needs prescriber review.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 records a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol (a change the standing order permits a clinic pharmacist to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery (1). His only current medication is levothyroxine; there is no current or prior anticoagulant order. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so untreated AF needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis and facial weakness. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), prior stroke (2), female (1). Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is ordered. Secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated - needs prescriber review.

Outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL with 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (order valid to 1/4/2027) and it is still listed as a current medication, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Continuation of the anticoagulant after a recent major GI bleed, without documentation that the bleeding source was treated and the risk/benefit reassessed, needs clinical review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was also re-issued the same day and remains valid to 1/3/2027. Both orders cover the evaluation date 9/24/2026, so the patient is on concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban - a duplicate-anticoagulation hazard that requires immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 134-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings, and the chart needs correction/review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus bradycardia at 62/min with QT 545 ms and Bazett QTc 554 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a watch-list drug, with a current order valid to 1/9/2027. Most recent electrolytes (6/9/2026) are potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at about 58/min with a markedly prolonged QT of 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and has been continuously prescribed since 2022. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, upright P wave before every QRS in lead II. PR 176 ms, QRS 82 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT 348 ms with Bazett QTc 385 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). Compared with the previous tracing of 11/21/2025 (105362569, sinus at 67/min with QT 497 ms, QTc 526 ms) the QTc has fallen by about 140 ms, a decrease of 60 ms or more; rhythm, intervals and axis are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS in lead II. PR about 130 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 307 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms, frontal axis about +2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 103/min (RR intervals 408-900 ms). No organised P waves are present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 72 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 314 ms, Bazett QTc about 411 ms using the mean RR. Frontal QRS axis about -58 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. The atrial fibrillation is consistent with the documented diagnosis; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 184 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 383 ms, Bazett QTc 359 ms, frontal axis about -10 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 12/13/2018 (108651109, sinus 66/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58/min. Upright P waves precede each QRS with a PR of about 178 ms; QRS 82 ms (narrow). The QT is markedly prolonged at 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG of 4/6/2022 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid irregular response at about 129/min and QTc 447 ms, the atrial fibrillation has resolved (organised sinus activity now present) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. The marked QT prolongation on long-term amiodarone is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS. PR about 132 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 498 ms with Bazett QTc 531 ms - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910, sinus at 75/min, QT 317 ms, QTc 353 ms) the QTc has increased by about 180 ms, far more than 60 ms. This ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable' on 5/14/2024 when escitalopram was started; the prolonged QTc on a QT watch-list drug is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II preceding each QRS. PR about 160 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms, frontal axis about +52 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is regular at about 141/min (RR 404-444 ms) and the baseline shows continuous, regular flutter activity at roughly twice the ventricular rate (about 280-290/min), best seen as the undulating sawtooth in leads II, III and V1; there are no discrete isoelectric-separated P waves, so no PR interval is reported. QRS 76 ms (narrow), QT 271 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal). The previous tracing of 7/11/2022 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular response at about 107/min and QTc 425 ms, so the rhythm has organised from atrial fibrillation into atrial flutter; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 429 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG of 3/18/2025 (101016166, sinus 102/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 428 ms) the tracing is unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 139/min (RR 348-650 ms). No P waves are identifiable and the baseline is fibrillatory, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 84 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 285 ms, Bazett QTc about 434 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 134/min with QTc 442 ms, so there is no interval change. Note the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' on this date, which these tracings contradict; that discrepancy is flagged separately.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, regular, with an upright P wave in lead II preceding each QRS. The PR interval is about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal (relatively long for this heart rate but not diagnostic of AV block). QRS 84 ms, QT 273 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms, frontal axis about +51 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980, sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a broad but upright P wave in lead II and a negative terminal component in V1 (left atrial abnormality, in keeping with the known mitral valve disease). PR about 165 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -41 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/16/2021 (102616671, sinus at 87/min, QTc 387 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction abnormality and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Regular atrial rhythm at about 70/min with a constant PR of roughly 150 ms and one late atrial premature beat. The P waves are low amplitude and negative in II, III and aVF with a positive vector in I/aVL, suggesting a low atrial (ectopic) focus rather than true high sinus node origin, but there is 1:1 atrial-ventricular conduction throughout. QRS 68 ms (narrow), QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms, frontal QRS axis about -27 degrees (within the normal range). Compared with the prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242, similar rhythm at 60/min, QTc 403 ms; that tracing shows arm-lead reversal) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Regular rhythm at 69/min with 1:1 atrial activity preceding each QRS at a PR of about 126 ms. QRS 84 ms (narrow), QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms. The measured frontal QRS axis is about -172 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant, with a deeply negative QRS and inverted P wave in lead I, positive complexes in aVR and normal R-wave progression in the precordial leads - the pattern strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeating the tracing with correct lead placement is advised. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 70/min (RR 462-1154 ms) and no discernible P waves, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 82 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 435 ms, Bazett QTc about 471 ms. Frontal axis about +27 degrees (normal). The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with QTc 384 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (amiodarone was being loaded at the time).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS (upright in II, negative in V1). PR about 138 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 417 ms, Bazett QTc 445 ms - upper normal but below the 500 ms review threshold. Frontal axis about +69 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible; it was obtained 3/8/2026 as the required post-escitalopram tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 190 ms (upper normal), QRS 82 ms, QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms, frontal axis about +49 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, regular, with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS. PR about 134 ms, QRS 86 ms (now narrow), QT 287 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The frontal QRS axis is about +177 degrees (right axis deviation, close to the extreme quadrant). Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (106516875, 12/5/2024 01:33) which showed a QRS of 144 ms with an rSR' and tall broad terminal R in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - a right bundle branch block - the QRS has normalised, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc fell from about 469 ms to 409 ms, a change of approximately 60 ms that is largely explained by loss of the bundle branch block and the faster rate.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 148/min (RR 316-602 ms). No organised P waves, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 258 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms. Frontal axis about -11 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 9/12/2025 (107374881) showed a regular rhythm at about 77/min with P waves and QTc 411 ms, so the atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is essentially unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 81/min with mild rate variation, upright P waves in lead II preceding every QRS. PR about 188 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 321 ms, Bazett QTc 372 ms, frontal axis about +37 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block; no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented history. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. It confirms the 3/7/2026 clinic note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 507 ms with Bazett QTc 548 ms - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis about +44 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/17/2020 (107149156, regular narrow-complex rhythm at 132/min with QTc 401 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The prolonged QTc on high-dose citalopram is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 65/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II before each QRS. PR about 162 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 381 ms. The frontal QRS axis is about -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min with a P wave before each QRS (positive in II, negative terminal deflection in V1). PR 124 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 328 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 (100698634) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QT about 270 ms and QTc about 425 ms, so there is no change in rhythm and the QTc change is under 60 ms. Note that despite the documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 118 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 423 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms, frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 3/8/2025 (106045460, sinus 62/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 441 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Note this tracing predates the haloperidol started 9/15/2026, so a new baseline ECG is required.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular, with a P wave preceding every QRS. PR about 148 ms, QRS 96 ms (slightly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block), QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 429 ms, frontal axis about +32 degrees (normal). No AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 176 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 319 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms, frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 7/27/2019 (107274479, sinus at 75/min, QRS 64 ms, QTc 415 ms) there is no change in rhythm or conduction and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at about 60/min with 1:1 upright P waves and a prolonged PR interval of roughly 222 ms (first-degree AV block). The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a QS complex in V1-V2 and a broad notched monophasic R wave in I, V5 and V6 with absent septal q waves - left bundle branch block. QT 446 ms, Bazett QTc 450 ms (in part rate- and LBBB-related). Frontal QRS axis about -23 degrees (within the normal range). The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 (103686933) showed the identical pattern - sinus rhythm, PR about 215 ms, QRS 124 ms LBBB, QTc 445 ms - so there is no new conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 126 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 319 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in lead II. PR about 166 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 401 ms, Bazett QTc 453 ms (upper normal, below the 500 ms threshold). Frontal axis about +62 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2/2/2020 (109048192, sinus at 75/min with inverted T waves, QT 456 ms, QTc 509 ms) the QTc has fallen by roughly 55 ms - less than the 60 ms threshold - and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, with a P wave preceding each QRS. PR about 134 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms, frontal axis about +20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible; it predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min with one atrial premature beat; each QRS is preceded by a P wave. The PR interval is prolonged at about 206 ms, consistent with (borderline) first-degree AV block. QRS 90 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -35 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. No atrial fibrillation is captured on this tracing despite the documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS. PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms (narrow), QT markedly prolonged at 545 ms with Bazett QTc 554 ms. Frontal axis about +66 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865, sinus bradycardia with occasional atrial ectopy, QT 459 ms, QTc about 432 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone therapy started 11/10/2025. The prolonged QTc on a QT watch-list drug is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular, with a discrete P wave before each QRS. PR about 170 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 288 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms, frontal axis about +31 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 7/4/2022 (102955795, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Despite the documented atrial flutter this tracing shows organised sinus activity.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular, with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS. PR about 182 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 429 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882, sinus at 57/min with a single atrial premature beat, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Notably there is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented history.

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min with 1:1 upright P waves in lead II. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT 398 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms, frontal axis about -4 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG of 11/30/2024 (103042067, sinus at 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QTc 360 ms) the PR is marginally longer but there is no new bundle branch block, no arrhythmia and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave preceding every QRS (upright in II, biphasic in V1). PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 309 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms, frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with normal upright P waves in lead II. PR about 152 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms, frontal axis about +54 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier on the same day (102910502, sinus 100/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 401 ms) and is essentially identical - no interval or rhythm change.

Continuation of the anticoagulant after a recent major GI bleed, without documentation that the bleeding source was treated and the risk/benefit reassessed, needs clinical review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was also re-issued the same day and remains valid to 1/3/2027. Both orders cover the evaluation date 9/24/2026, so the patient is on concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban - a duplicate-anticoagulation hazard that requires immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 134-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings, and the chart needs correction/review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus bradycardia at 62/min with QT 545 ms and Bazett QTc 554 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a watch-list drug, with a current order valid to 1/9/2027. Most recent electrolytes (6/9/2026) are potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at about 58/min with a markedly prolonged QT of 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and has been continuously prescribed since 2022. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, upright P wave before every QRS in lead II. PR 176 ms, QRS 82 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT 348 ms with Bazett QTc 385 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). Compared with the previous tracing of 11/21/2025 (105362569, sinus at 67/min with QT 497 ms, QTc 526 ms) the QTc has fallen by about 140 ms, a decrease of 60 ms or more; rhythm, intervals and axis are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS in lead II. PR about 130 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 307 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms, frontal axis about +2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 103/min (RR intervals 408-900 ms). No organised P waves are present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 72 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 314 ms, Bazett QTc about 411 ms using the mean RR. Frontal QRS axis about -58 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. The atrial fibrillation is consistent with the documented diagnosis; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 184 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 383 ms, Bazett QTc 359 ms, frontal axis about -10 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 12/13/2018 (108651109, sinus 66/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58/min. Upright P waves precede each QRS with a PR of about 178 ms; QRS 82 ms (narrow). The QT is markedly prolonged at 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG of 4/6/2022 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid irregular response at about 129/min and QTc 447 ms, the atrial fibrillation has resolved (organised sinus activity now present) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. The marked QT prolongation on long-term amiodarone is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS. PR about 132 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 498 ms with Bazett QTc 531 ms - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910, sinus at 75/min, QT 317 ms, QTc 353 ms) the QTc has increased by about 180 ms, far more than 60 ms. This ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable' on 5/14/2024 when escitalopram was started; the prolonged QTc on a QT watch-list drug is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II preceding each QRS. PR about 160 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms, frontal axis about +52 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is regular at about 141/min (RR 404-444 ms) and the baseline shows continuous, regular flutter activity at roughly twice the ventricular rate (about 280-290/min), best seen as the undulating sawtooth in leads II, III and V1; there are no discrete isoelectric-separated P waves, so no PR interval is reported. QRS 76 ms (narrow), QT 271 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal). The previous tracing of 7/11/2022 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular response at about 107/min and QTc 425 ms, so the rhythm has organised from atrial fibrillation into atrial flutter; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in lead II. PR about 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 429 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG of 3/18/2025 (101016166, sinus 102/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 428 ms) the tracing is unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 139/min (RR 348-650 ms). No P waves are identifiable and the baseline is fibrillatory, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 84 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 285 ms, Bazett QTc about 434 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 134/min with QTc 442 ms, so there is no interval change. Note the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' on this date, which these tracings contradict; that discrepancy is flagged separately.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, regular, with an upright P wave in lead II preceding each QRS. The PR interval is about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal (relatively long for this heart rate but not diagnostic of AV block). QRS 84 ms, QT 273 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms, frontal axis about +51 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980, sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a broad but upright P wave in lead II and a negative terminal component in V1 (left atrial abnormality, in keeping with the known mitral valve disease). PR about 165 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -41 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/16/2021 (102616671, sinus at 87/min, QTc 387 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction abnormality and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Regular atrial rhythm at about 70/min with a constant PR of roughly 150 ms and one late atrial premature beat. The P waves are low amplitude and negative in II, III and aVF with a positive vector in I/aVL, suggesting a low atrial (ectopic) focus rather than true high sinus node origin, but there is 1:1 atrial-ventricular conduction throughout. QRS 68 ms (narrow), QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms, frontal QRS axis about -27 degrees (within the normal range). Compared with the prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242, similar rhythm at 60/min, QTc 403 ms; that tracing shows arm-lead reversal) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Regular rhythm at 69/min with 1:1 atrial activity preceding each QRS at a PR of about 126 ms. QRS 84 ms (narrow), QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms. The measured frontal QRS axis is about -172 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant, with a deeply negative QRS and inverted P wave in lead I, positive complexes in aVR and normal R-wave progression in the precordial leads - the pattern strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeating the tracing with correct lead placement is advised. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 70/min (RR 462-1154 ms) and no discernible P waves, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 82 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT about 435 ms, Bazett QTc about 471 ms. Frontal axis about +27 degrees (normal). The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with QTc 384 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (amiodarone was being loaded at the time).

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min with a P wave before each QRS (positive in II, negative terminal deflection in V1). PR 124 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 328 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 (100698634) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QT about 270 ms and QTc about 425 ms, so there is no change in rhythm and the QTc change is under 60 ms. Note that despite the documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS. PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms (narrow), QT markedly prolonged at 545 ms with Bazett QTc 554 ms. Frontal axis about +66 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865, sinus bradycardia with occasional atrial ectopy, QT 459 ms, QTc about 432 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone therapy started 11/10/2025. The prolonged QTc on a QT watch-list drug is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular, with a discrete P wave before each QRS. PR about 170 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 288 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms, frontal axis about +31 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 7/4/2022 (102955795, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Despite the documented atrial flutter this tracing shows organised sinus activity.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular, with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS. PR about 182 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 429 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882, sinus at 57/min with a single atrial premature beat, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Notably there is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented history.

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min with 1:1 upright P waves in lead II. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QT 398 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms, frontal axis about -4 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG of 11/30/2024 (103042067, sinus at 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QTc 360 ms) the PR is marginally longer but there is no new bundle branch block, no arrhythmia and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave preceding every QRS (upright in II, biphasic in V1). PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 309 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms, frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with normal upright P waves in lead II. PR about 152 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms, frontal axis about +54 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier on the same day (102910502, sinus 100/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 401 ms) and is essentially identical - no interval or rhythm change.

items.explanation: 48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure 1, hypertension 1; age 48 = 0, no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease, male). Current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only - there is no current anticoagulant order and none has ever been prescribed in clinic. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation in the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, so this untreated AF needs prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is current, most recently reordered 7/18/2026 and valid to 12/26/2026; it was in fact started on 5/14/2024 after this ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable'. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026). Prescriber review of escitalopram, with a repeat ECG, is required.

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 507 ms and Bazett QTc 548 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Citalopram 40 mg daily - a QT watch-list drug, and a dose above the 20 mg maximum advised in older/at-risk patients - is current (order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The memo in force for starts on or after 9/1/2025 requires an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. Because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The revised memo applies to starts on or after 3/1/2026 and requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. The revised memo (starts on or after 3/1/2026) requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not obtained until 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met in time and is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. No ECG is present in the chart. However the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 (5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, would fall inside the window, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start; no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), hypertension (1), age 80 (2), type 2 diabetes (1), prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual hemiplegia and dysarthria (2), old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis (1), female (1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant is ordered. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF - oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated and this needs prescriber review.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 records a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol (a change the standing order permits a clinic pharmacist to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery (1). His only current medication is levothyroxine; there is no current or prior anticoagulant order. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so untreated AF needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis and facial weakness. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), prior stroke (2), female (1). Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is ordered. Secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated - needs prescriber review.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58/min. Upright P waves precede each QRS with a PR of about 178 ms; QRS 82 ms (narrow). The QT is markedly prolonged at 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms. The previous tracing of 7/11/2022 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular response at about 107/min and QTc 425 ms, so the rhythm has organised from atrial fibrillation into atrial flutter; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980, sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a broad but upright P wave in lead II and a negative terminal component in V1 (left atrial abnormality, in keeping with the known mitral valve disease). Regular atrial rhythm at about 70/min with a constant PR of roughly 150 ms and one late atrial premature beat. Compared with the prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242, similar rhythm at 60/min, QTc 403 ms; that tracing shows arm-lead reversal) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Regular rhythm at 69/min with 1:1 atrial activity preceding each QRS at a PR of about 126 ms. QRS 84 ms (narrow), QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

The frontal QRS axis is about +177 degrees (right axis deviation, close to the extreme quadrant). QTc fell from about 469 ms to 409 ms, a change of approximately 60 ms that is largely explained by loss of the bundle branch block and the faster rate.

Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF - oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated and this needs prescriber review.

Both orders cover the evaluation date 9/24/2026, so the patient is on concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban - a duplicate-anticoagulation hazard that requires immediate reconciliation.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response averaging about 139/min (RR 348-650 ms). items.explanation: 48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure 1, hypertension 1; age 48 = 0, no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease, male). Current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only - there is no current anticoagulant order and none has ever been prescribed in clinic. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation in the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, so this untreated AF needs prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is current, most recently reordered 7/18/2026 and valid to 12/26/2026; it was in fact started on 5/14/2024 after this ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable'. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026). Prescriber review of escitalopram, with a repeat ECG, is required.

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 507 ms and Bazett QTc 548 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Citalopram 40 mg daily - a QT watch-list drug, and a dose above the 20 mg maximum advised in older/at-risk patients - is current (order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The memo in force for starts on or after 9/1/2025 requires an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The revised memo applies to starts on or after 3/1/2026 and requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. The revised memo (starts on or after 3/1/2026) requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not obtained until 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met in time and is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. No ECG is present in the chart. However the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 (5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, would fall inside the window, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start; no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), hypertension (1), age 80 (2), type 2 diabetes (1), prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual hemiplegia and dysarthria (2), old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis (1), female (1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant is ordered. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF - oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated and this needs prescriber review.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 records a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol (a change the standing order permits a clinic pharmacist to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery (1). His only current medication is levothyroxine; there is no current or prior anticoagulant order. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so untreated AF needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis and facial weakness. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension (1), age 71 (1), prior stroke (2), female (1). Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is ordered. Secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated - needs prescriber review.

Outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL with 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (order valid to 1/4/2027) and it is still listed as a current medication, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Continuation of the anticoagulant after a recent major GI bleed, without documentation that the bleeding source was treated and the risk/benefit reassessed, needs clinical review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was also re-issued the same day and remains valid to 1/3/2027. Both orders cover the evaluation date 9/24/2026, so the patient is on concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban - a duplicate-anticoagulation hazard that requires immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 134-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings, and the chart needs correction/review.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus bradycardia at 62/min with QT 545 ms and Bazett QTc 554 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a watch-list drug, with a current order valid to 1/9/2027. Most recent electrolytes (6/9/2026) are potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at about 58/min with a markedly prolonged QT of 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and has been continuously prescribed since 2022. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.
